title: Network threads let deterministic models produce quantum correlations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Network threads let deterministic models produce quantum correlations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The quantum correlations between distant particles usually taken to rule out definite underlying processes can arise in a deterministic network model, because particles created together stay linked by threads of connections that bypass ordinary three-dimensional space.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And the basic reason for this is that if the universe is a network then it can in a sense easily contain threads that continue to connect particles even when the particles get far apart in terms of ordinary space.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Quantum Phenomena” (from p. 537), p. 544. Scope: correlations in measurements on entangled particle pairs (Bell-type experiments)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-27: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public Bell-test results allow quantitative comparison and a constructive model can establish logical possibility. Such agreement would not show that physical entanglement is caused by network threads, so the mechanistic claim remains only partially resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Construct a deterministic network model with persistent non-spatial links and derive its conditional outcome probabilities for loophole-free Bell experiments. Matching the full correlations while preserving the model's stated causal assumptions supports possibility; violation of Bell bounds only refutes models satisfying the corresponding locality and independence assumptions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Many models can reproduce correlations without identifying nature's mechanism.

Network threads amount to nonlocal structure and may evade rather than explain Bell assumptions.

Measurement independence and no-signalling must be checked.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bell-type correlations are measured and publicly documented, so the phenomenon the mechanism is meant to explain is not in doubt. The thread explanation is an existence claim about deterministic networks, and no public model is tight enough that the measured correlations confirm or refute it rather than quantum theory in general. Only the empirical half is currently testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare measured correlations of entangled pairs with the quantum predictions, and separately exhibit a deterministic network whose extra-spatial threads reproduce those correlations, including the strength of the violation. A working thread model confirms the possibility claim; measured correlations are already known and do not by themselves test the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Standard quantum mechanics and other deterministic hidden-variable pictures with extra connections fit the same correlations.

An existence claim ('can arise') is confirmed only by an explicit model and is barely refuted by unsuccessful attempts.
